stem.en: A town stands on a coast where the cliff moves back a little every year. A tourist beach lies further along the same shore. Which statement is true?

text.en: The town may need protection; the beach brings tourists.

feedback.en: Right. Different stretches of one coast can matter in different ways.

text.en: The town is safe, because cliffs never move.

feedback.en: Waves wear a cliff back over time.

text.en: The beach has no use, because it is only sand.

feedback.en: Beaches support tourism and fishing and act as natural barriers.

text.en: Waves will soon stop, because the cliff is made of hard rock.

feedback.en: Waves keep working. Hard rock only wears away more slowly.

explanation.en: A retreating cliff can put buildings at risk, so a settlement may need coastal protection. A beach can bring tourists and also acts as a natural barrier.

hints.en: Think about what each part of the coast does for people.
